title: AFCAT Exam Guide: Flying, Technical & Ground Duty Officer Careers, AFSB & Free Study Material
summary: Everything you need to crack the Air Force Common Admission Test (AFCAT) for men and women: branch-wise eligibility, exam weightage graph, 5-day AFSB interview breakdown, CPSS testing, pay matrix, and free mock tests.
author: Sarkari Aavedan Editorial Team
content:
## Introduction & Career Overview

The Air Force Common Admission Test (**AFCAT**) is conducted twice annually by the Indian Air Force (IAF) through C-DAC to recruit dynamic graduate men and women as Commissioned Class-I Gazetted Officers. Commissioning into the IAF offers exceptional leadership opportunities across the **Flying Branch (Fighter, Transport, and Helicopter Pilots)**, **Ground Duty (Technical)**, and **Ground Duty (Non-Technical)** branches. Successful candidates undergo rigorous military training at the prestigious Air Force Academy (**AFA**) Dundigal, Hyderabad.

> [!IMPORTANT]  
> Indian Air Force commissions both male and female candidates through AFCAT for Permanent Commission (PC) and Short Service Commission (SSC). Women officers are fully eligible for combat flying streams including Rafale, Su-30MKI, and Tejas fighter squadrons.

## Branch-Wise Eligibility & Age Criteria

| IAF Branch | Permissible Age Limit | Mandatory Educational Qualifications | Minimum Aggregate Score Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Flying Branch** | 20 – 24 Years (Up to 26 for valid DGCA CPL holders) | Graduate in any discipline with min 60% marks **AND** passed 10+2 with min 50% marks each in **Maths and Physics** OR B.E./B.Tech degree with min 60% marks. | 60% in Graduation & 50% in 10+2 Maths & Physics |
| **Ground Duty (Technical) - AE(L) Electronics** | 20 – 26 Years | 10+2 with min 50% marks in Physics and Mathematics **AND** 4-year B.E./B.Tech degree in Electronics, Communication, Electrical, Computer Science, or equivalent. | Min 60% aggregate in Engineering degree |
| **Ground Duty (Technical) - AE(M) Mechanical** | 20 – 26 Years | 10+2 with min 50% in Physics & Maths **AND** 4-year B.E./B.Tech degree in Mechanical, Aerospace, Aeronautical, Metallurgy, Production, or Industrial Engineering. | Min 60% aggregate in Engineering degree |
| **Weapon Systems (WS) Branch** | 20 – 26 Years | Graduate in any discipline with min 60% marks **AND** passed 10+2 with min 50% marks each in Mathematics and Physics. | 60% Graduation + 50% in 10+2 Maths/Physics |
| **Administration & Logistics** | 20 – 26 Years | Graduate in any discipline from a recognized University with minimum 60% marks or equivalent. | Min 60% aggregate score in Graduation |
| **Accounts Branch** | 20 – 26 Years | B.Com / B.B.A (Finance) / B.M.S / B.B.S / C.A. / C.M.A. with minimum 60% marks. | Min 60% in Commerce or Finance Graduation |
| **Education Branch** | 20 – 26 Years | 10+2 and Post-Graduation with 50% in English / Physics / Math / Chemistry / History / Geography AND 60% in Graduation. | 50% in PG + 60% in UG |

## Step-by-Step Selection Procedure

1. Register online during the application window on the official C-DAC AFCAT portal (afcat.cdac.in).
2. Appear for the Computer Based Online Written Examination (AFCAT) consisting of 100 objective questions for 300 marks.
3. Check official cut-off marks and select your preferred Air Force Selection Board (AFSB) venue and testing date via the candidate dashboard.
4. Attend the 5-Day AFSB Interview Testing Process at Dehradun (1 AFSB), Mysuru (2 AFSB), Gandhinagar (3 AFSB), Varanasi (4 AFSB), or Guwahati (5 AFSB).
5. Undergo CPSS (Computerised Pilot Selection System) testing if recommended for the Flying Branch.
6. Undergo comprehensive military medical examination at AFCME New Delhi or IAM Bengaluru.
7. Await Final All India Merit List based on cumulative written and AFSB scores for admission to AFA Dundigal.

## AFCAT Examination Pattern & Mark Weightage

The AFCAT online examination consists of 100 questions for 300 marks. The test duration is 2 hours (120 minutes). Each correct answer awards **+3 marks**, while each incorrect answer penalizes **-1 mark**.

| Section / Subject | Questions | Marks | Mark Weightage Graph | High-Scoring Focus Topics |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Verbal Ability in English** | 30 Questions | 90 Marks | [BAR:30%:English Language] | Comprehension, Cloze Test, Error Detection, Idioms & Phrases, Synonyms, Antonyms |
| **Reasoning & Military Aptitude** | 30 Questions | 90 Marks | [BAR:30%:Reasoning & Aptitude] | Spatial Ability, Dot Situation, Figure Analogy, Embedded Figures, Venn Diagrams |
| **General Awareness** | 20 Questions | 60 Marks | [BAR:20%:General Awareness] | IAF Fighter Jets & Missiles, Defense Exercises, Modern History, Polity, Geography, Sports |
| **Numerical Ability (Mathematics)** | 20 Questions | 60 Marks | [BAR:20%:Numerical Ability] | Time & Work, Speed Distance Time, Percentage, Profit & Loss, Ratio, Averages, Trains |
| **Grand Total** | **100 Questions** | **300 Marks** | **[BAR:100%:Total Composite]** | **Composite Time: 120 Minutes (Cutoff: ~140–165 Marks)** |

> [!TIP]  
> **The 180-Mark Foundation**: Verbal Ability in English (90 marks) and Reasoning & Military Aptitude (90 marks) together contribute **180 out of 300 marks (60% weightage)**! Mastering these two sections alone guarantees clearing the written exam cutoff.

## The 5-Day AFSB Interview Breakdown

| Testing Day | Testing Stage | Assessment Activities & Procedure |
|---|---|---|
| **Day 1: Screening Stage** | Stage-I Testing | **Officer Intelligence Rating (OIR)** verbal/non-verbal test followed by **Picture Perception & Discussion Test (PPDT)**. Screened-in candidates stay for Stage-II; screened-out candidates return home the same afternoon. |
| **Day 2: Psychological Battery** | Stage-II Testing | Written psychological projection tests: **TAT** (12 stories on ambiguous slides), **WAT** (60 words in 15 mins), **SRT** (60 daily life situations in 30 mins), and **Self Description (SD)**. |
| **Day 3 & Day 4: Group Testing (GTO)** | Outdoor Leadership | **Group Discussion (GD)**, **Military Planning Exercise (GPE)**, **Progressive Group Task (PGT)**, **Half Group Task (HGT)**, **Command Task**, **Individual Obstacles (10 obstacles)**, and **Snake Race**. |
| **Day 3 or Day 4: Personal Interview** | One-on-One Interview | Comprehensive personal interaction with the Interviewing Officer (IO) testing background, family, education, current defense affairs, hobbies, and emotional maturity. |
| **Day 5: Board Conference** | Final Recommendation | All board assessors assemble. Each candidate appears for 1 to 5 minutes before the board. Final recommendations are declared immediately thereafter. |

## Computerised Pilot Selection System (CPSS)

> [!NOTE]  
> CPSS is a **once-in-a-lifetime test** administered strictly to candidates opting for the Flying Branch. If cleared, you remain permanently qualified for military flying in IAF, Navy, Army, and Coast Guard. If failed, you can never apply for military pilot entries again, but remain eligible for Ground Duty branches.

- **Part 1 (Instrument Battery Test)**: 90-minute computerized test assessing speed of cockpit instrument scanning and orientation interpretation.
- **Part 2 (Machine Sensor Test)**: Hand-and-foot cockpit simulator testing psychomotor reflexes, control stick coordination, and sensory multitasking.

## Flying Officer Salary & Allowances (7th CPC)

| Salary Parameter | Amount / Allowance per Month | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Pay Matrix Level** | **Level-10 (Defense Pay Matrix)** | Substantive rank of Flying Officer upon commissioning |
| **Basic Pay** | ₹56,100 / month | Annual incremental progression up to ₹1,77,500 |
| **Military Service Pay (MSP)** | ₹15,500 / month | Mandatory for all commissioned defense officers |
| **Flying Allowance** | ₹25,000 / month | Applicable to all commissioned Flying Branch officers |
| **Dearness Allowance (DA)** | ~50% of Basic + MSP (~₹35,800) | Revised semi-annually |
| **Transport & Kit Maintenance** | ₹7,200 + DA | Official transport maintenance compensation |
| **Approx Starting Gross Salary** | **₹1,15,000 – ₹1,35,000 / month** | Plus free furnished military accommodation, mess, and canteen (CSD) privileges |
